newsitem.title: GREECE: IMPLIED DRACHMA RATES FROM FORWARDS FIRM IN LATE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: IMPLIED DRACHMA RATES FROM FORWARDS FIRM IN LATE TRADE.

text.p: Implied drachma rates from forex forwards added another five to 10 basis points to their earlier levels on funding for bonds and FRNs to be auctioned on January 24 but interbank depos were holding, dealers said.

"Implied drachma rates from forex forwards have risen another five to 10 basis points depending on the period with short rates firmer than long ones," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Their firmness is directly linked to bond and FRN funding."

The finance ministry will hold an auction of 250 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters with the firsat coupon set at 12.40 percent and 120 billion drachma worth of three-year, 10.20 percent coupon bonds on January 24. The state collected about 230 billion drachmas from the sale of two-year zeros that were on sale on Monday. The two-year zero coupon note carried a gross yield to maturity of 10.30 percent.
Bond dealers said the market was very quiet with trading activity subdued despite news that set the terms of the auction on January 24.
Ecu/drachma was fluctuating in unexciting ranges throughout the day trading at 303.13/18 in late dealings.
The mark was quoted at 155.70/80 drachmas from Tuesday's 152.230 fix, the dollar at 252.53/63 drachmas from 252.230 and the Ecu at 303.08/18 from 302.980 drachmas.
